title: ABIDE-II feature correlation explorer
description: Course activity for Chapter 1 EDA: pick two numeric variables, choose Pearson or Spearman, and see the scatterplot, the pairwise-complete sample size, and how the relationship changes when you colour by diagnosis or sex.
instructions: Choose an X and a Y variable. Predict the direction and rough strength before you read the coefficient. Watch the pairwise-complete n: two coefficients in the same matrix can describe very different subsets of participants. Switch Pearson ↔ Spearman, and colour by a group to check whether an overall association survives within groups.
reflectionPrompts: Before reading the coefficient, predict the sign and rough strength, and sketch the shape you expect (a line? a cloud? a curve?).

Compare FIQ vs Verbal IQ with ADOS-G total vs ADOS-2 total. Both look strong — but check the pairwise-complete n. Which coefficient describes almost the whole sample, and which describes a small selected subset?
Full-scale IQ is built from Verbal and Performance IQ. Is a strong FIQ–VIQ correlation a finding about the brain, or a consequence of how the score is defined?

Colour FIQ vs SRS total by diagnostic group. The overall correlation is moderate and negative; what happens to it inside the Autism group and inside the Control group, and what does that tell you about the overall number?
A correlation — Pearson or Spearman — measures association, not causation. For a pair that correlates, name one third variable that could drive both.
